body: Self-evolving language models have recently emerged as a promising path toward superintelligence, with the advantage of reducing the cost of human supervision. While considerable progress has been made in verifiable domains, self-evolution in unverifiable domains remains substantially less explored. We propose Judge co-adaptation from Zero data (J-Zero), a unified Challenger--Solver--Judge co-evolution framework that supports self-improvement across both domains. The Challenger and Solver co-evolve through an adversarial interaction: the Challenger generates increasingly difficult tasks, while the Solver learns to produce higher-quality responses to them. In parallel, the Judge co-adapts using preference pairs whose ordering is known in advance from how each response was produced, i.e., the Solver's answer over the Challenger's, and its decomposed-and-recombined answer over its one-shot answer, rather than from the Judge's own scores. J-Zero outperforms the baselines by an average of 4.2 points on verifiable and 8.0 points on unverifiable domains, and continues to improve through at least ten iterations, whereas the baselines degrade after two.
summaryZh: 该研究提出了J-Zero，一个统一的“挑战者-求解者-裁判”协同演化框架，支持模型在零数据情况下进行自我改进，尤其是在不可验证领域。挑战者生成难度递增的任务，求解者学习生成更高质量的响应，而裁判则根据预知的偏好对进行协同适应，而非依赖自身评分。J-Zero在可验证和不可验证领域均显著优于基线模型，并能持续改进，而基线模型在几轮后即开始退化。

glossary.explanationZh: 能够通过与环境交互或自我生成数据来持续改进自身性能的语言模型。
指在训练或评估过程中，模型不接触任何与特定任务相关的标注数据。
一种用于模型自我改进的框架，其中挑战者生成任务，求解者完成任务，裁判评估其表现。
指那些难以客观评估模型输出正确性的领域，例如创意写作或开放式对话。
